quiz.title: Module 2 — Tuesday — Writing Social Media Posts and Captions
quiz.description: Tuesday's quiz covers writing concisely for people who skim, encouraging conversation on Facebook, using capitalisation and emojis well, and the hashtag and hook advice for Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, why should social media writers aim to communicate their message in as few words as possible?
options: Longer posts are not allowed on social media platforms.
People often scroll or skim quickly, so concise writing helps capture their attention.
Short posts do not require correct grammar or spelling.
Short posts automatically receive more likes and comments.
questions.explanation: The feed is read at speed. Tight writing gives a skimming reader the point before they move on; length is not what makes a post land.

questions.prompt: When writing a Facebook caption, which approach can help encourage engagement and conversation?
options: Using as many hashtags as possible.
Writing only about the products or services being sold.
Opening with an interesting question or story and inviting the audience to respond.
Avoiding replies to comments so the post can reach more people.
questions.explanation: Facebook rewards discussion. A question or story gives people something to answer, and a direct invitation tells them that responding is welcome.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, what is the recommended way to use capitalization to make important words stand out in social media posts?
options: Write every important word entirely in capital letters.
Capitalize the first letter of selected important words.
Capitalize every word in the post.
Avoid capitalization because it makes posts difficult to read.
questions.explanation: Capitalising the first letter of a chosen word gives it weight without shouting. A whole post in capitals reads as aggressive and slows the reader down.

questions.prompt: Which hashtag strategy does the second video recommend for Instagram captions?
options: Use all 30 hashtags Instagram allows on every post.
Avoid hashtags completely because they never help content get discovered.
Use long, general hashtags to attract the widest possible audience.
Use one or two relevant hashtags to target a specific audience.
questions.explanation: A small number of precise hashtags puts the post in front of the people it is actually for, rather than burying it in a crowded general feed.

questions.prompt: Why does the second video recommend beginning LinkedIn captions with an intriguing hook?
options: It encourages readers to click "see more" and continue reading.
It allows users to publish without writing a complete message.
It guarantees that every reader will follow the account.
It removes the need to include a call to action.
questions.explanation: LinkedIn truncates longer posts behind "see more". The opening line has to earn that click, or the rest of the post is never read.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, what is the best way to use emojis in social media posts?
options: Avoid them on every platform because they look unprofessional.
Use as many as possible to make every post entertaining.
Use them appropriately to add color, fun, and emotion without overusing them.
Replace written words with emojis whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Emojis work as seasoning — a little adds warmth and tone. Piled on, they compete with the words and make the post harder to read.

questions.prompt: A business is posting a new product announcement on Twitter (X). According to the second video, which approach would make the caption more effective?
options: Copy the product title exactly and use several long hashtags.
Keep the caption short and simple, and tease the announcement with an interesting detail.
Write a long article explaining every feature of the product.
Avoid including links or calls to action.
questions.explanation: X moves fast. A short caption with one intriguing detail gives people a reason to look, where a full feature list or a wall of hashtags gets scrolled past.

questions.prompt: A house-cleaning business wants to attract TikTok users who are specifically interested in its services. Which hashtag approach best follows the second video's advice?
options: Use only broad hashtags such as #business and #popular.
Use as many unrelated trending hashtags as possible.
Use the same broad hashtags for every type of business.
Use specific, niche hashtags such as #housecleaning to connect with a relevant audience.
questions.explanation: Niche tags describe what the viewer is actually looking for. Broad or unrelated trending tags reach more people who care less about the service.
